extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / anabelian geometry (readers of Mochizuki's IUT series)
extracted.subtask_description: Developing the inter-universal Teichmüller theory structures: constructing Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters, their associated D-versions and base categories, and assembling them into Θ-links, Frobenius- and étale-pictures for use in Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater (and D-version)
rubrics_metrics.description: From initial Θ-data one may construct a Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater — in essence, a system of Frobenioids — and an associated D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater; these determine associated base categories (the system of base categories associated to the system of Frobenioids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction is effected from the Θ-data (EF, F, l, V) as in the discussion; see Deﬁnition 6.13 for the precise formal construction. The D-version and the base-category system are part of the package and should be produced together with the Frobenioid system.

rubrics_metrics.name: F(cid:3)±_l-symmetry (global portion structure and labels)
rubrics_metrics.description: The global portion of a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater consists of a category equivalent to the full subcategory determined by the connected objects of the Galois category of finite étale coverings of the (orbi)curve X_K and is equipped with an F(cid:3)±-symmetry, i.e., a poly-action by F(cid:3)± on the labels l (−l(cid:2) < ... < −1 < 0 < 1 < ... < l(cid:2)), each represented in the D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater by a D-prime-strip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building the global portion regard labels as elements ∈ F_l represented by D-prime-strips; analogous statements hold for the D-ΘNF-Hodge theater with its l-symmetry. In gluing operations identify labels (e.g., 0 = ±t ∈ F_l) across the respective symmetries as specified (cf. Proposition 6.7; Remark 6.12.2; Fig. 6.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of Θ-links (full poly-isomorphism of prime-strips)
rubrics_metrics.description: By taking appropriate roots of q-parameters of the elliptic curve at bad places and extending to satisfy the product formula, and by considering reciprocal l-th roots of the Frobenioid-theoretic theta function, one constructs natural F(cid:4)-prime-strips associated to a Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater. The full poly-isomorphism (the collection of all isomorphisms between these F(cid:4)-prime-strips) is the Θ-link between two Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Θ-link is the full poly-isomorphism between the F(cid:4)-prime-strip mods of the two theaters; it induces the full poly-isomorphism between the associated F(cid:4)×-prime-strips. Construction must respect the product formula and the reciprocity/root choices described (cf. Deﬁnitions 3.6, 5.2 and Corollary 3.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius-picture (infinite Θ-linked chain and symmetry constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: An indexed collection {nHT Θ±ellNF}n∈Z of distinct Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters linked by Θ-links forms the Frobenius-picture: an infinite chain ... → (n−1)HT → nHT → (n+1)HT → .... The Frobenius-picture fails to admit permutation automorphisms that switch adjacent indices n, n+1 while fixing the rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Frobenius-picture induces an infinite chain of full poly-isomorphisms between the associated D(cid:4)-prime-strips and F(cid:4)×-prime-strips. When analyzing automorphisms note the forbidden adjacent-index swaps; this asymmetry is central to subsequent constructions (cf. Corollary 3.8 and Fig. I1.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Étale-picture (relations to mono-analytic core and permutation symmetries)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relationships of the D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters to a mono-analytic core constituted by a distinguished D(cid:4)-prime-strip are depicted by spokes (Fig. I1.6) and are compatible with arbitrary permutation symmetries among the spokes (i.e., among the labels n ∈ Z of the D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters). This diagram is referred to as the étale-picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Frobenius-picture forbids adjacent transpositions, the étale-picture allows arbitrary permutations among the spokes; use this distinction when interpreting symmetry phenomena and when relating D-prime-strip isomorphisms (cf. Corollaries 4.12(ii), 6.10(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperered-profinite containment/equality criterion (Theorem B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Πtp_X be the tempered fundamental group of a hyperbolic curve X over a mixed-characteristic local field k and (cid:10)ΠX its étale fundamental group (the profinite completion). Every decomposition (respectively inertia) group in (cid:10)ΠX associated to a closed point or cusp is contained in Πtp_X iff it is a decomposition (resp. inertia) group in Πtp_X. Moreover, a (cid:10)ΠX-conjugate of Πtp_X contains such a decomposition (resp. inertia) group in Πtp_X iff it equals Πtp_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement (Theorem B / Corollary 2.5) provides the precise criterion for when profinite decomposition/inertia groups correspond to tempered ones; it holds without the stable-reduction assumption (the latter can be removed by Proposition 2.4(iii)). Use this to relate profinite conjugacy classes to tempered conjugacy classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of Theorem B for ±-indeterminacy synchronization
rubrics_metrics.description: The F(cid:3)±-symmetry depends crucially on synchronization of ±-indeterminacies occurring locally at each v ∈ V; such synchronization can only be obtained by using the global portion of the Θ±ell-Hodge theater and, in order to relate global profinite conjugacy classes to corresponding tempered conjugacy classes of inertia groups at v ∈ Vbad (where Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation is performed), one must apply Theorem B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performing Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluations that rely on ±-synchronizations, explicitly invoke Theorem B to pass between profinite and tempered conjugacy classes (see Remark 4.5.1 and [IUTchII], Remark 2.5.2 for detailed discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing via poly-isomorphisms lies outside conventional scheme theory
rubrics_metrics.description: The gluing isomorphisms (correspondences nΘ_v → (n+1)q_v) used to form the Frobenius-picture do not arise from ring homomorphisms; although each model nHT Θ±ellNF is constructed within conventional scheme theory, the relationships between distinct models cannot be expressed scheme-theoretically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat such gluing operations as genuinely non-scheme-theoretic filters: their geometry and arithmetic cannot be encoded by ordinary morphisms of schemes. This is a foundational feature; do not attempt to force a scheme-theoretic description of the inter-model gluing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of Frobenioid monoids enables gluing (monoid structure requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The possibility of the non-scheme-theoretic gluings rests on the relatively simple structure of the Frobenioid-like monoids involved (e.g., collections of monoids isomorphic to N or R_{≥0}); this relative simplicity (compared to ring structure) is essential to effect gluing across theaters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When formulating or applying gluing correspondences, explicitly identify and use the monoid/Frobenioid structures (their being essentially N or R_{≥0}-like) which make the gluings tractable; the inability to mirror ring-theoretic complexity is part of the mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer-theory uniqueness under Galois-compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Although one might try other correspondences to specify monoids/Frobenioids within each Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater, the rigidity of the relevant local and global monoids with Galois actions implies that, if one imposes the natural condition of Galois-compatibility, the correspondence furnished by Kummer theory is the only acceptable choice for constructing the required precise specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing the correspondence to specify the monoids/Frobenioids in a Galois-compatible way, use Kummer-theory classes; attempts to replace Kummer theory (without violating Galois-compatibility) will fail due to rigidity (cf. Corollary 5.3(i,ii,iv) and [IUTchII], Remark 3.6.2(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of absolute anabelian geometry to analyze Frobenius-picture (reconstruction requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describing an alien 'arithmetic holomorphic structure' corresponding to one Hodge theater in terms of a known arithmetic holomorphic structure corresponding to another (i.e., analyzing the Frobenius-picture) requires applying results from absolute anabelian geometry — e.g., theories developed in [SemiAnbd], [EtTh], and [AbsTopIII] — concerning reconstruction of ring/scheme structures from fundamental-group data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach the problem of reconstructing or describing alien arithmetic holomorphic structures by applying absolute anabelian reconstruction techniques: consider the profinite/non-profinite fundamental groups and their automorphisms, interpret Galois groups as arithmetic tangent bundles, and use H^1-type deformation analyses as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-universal principle: only abstract topological group survives non-ring filters
rubrics_metrics.description: In passing across non-ring/scheme-theoretic filters (like Θ-links or log-links), the only type of mathematical object that makes sense simultaneously in domain and codomain is the notion of the underlying abstract topological group of an étale fundamental group; auxiliary basepoint/fiber-functor data does not transport across such filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relating structures across non-ring filters, restrict attention to the abstract topological group underlying the étale fundamental group (forget the scheme-basepoint incarnation). Constructions relying on basepoint-determined fiber functors will not be directly transportable across the filter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate synchronization of local Galois groups (requirement and role)
rubrics_metrics.description: An important inter-universal phenomenon is conjugate synchronization: synchronization between conjugacy indeterminacies of distinct copies of various local Galois groups; this synchronization (together with rigidity properties of the étale theta function) plays a crucial role in the later theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement mechanisms to synchronize conjugacy indeterminacies when comparing local Galois data across theaters; use rigidity results (e.g., étale theta function rigidity from [EtTh]) to effect this synchronization in a Galois-compatible manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta-vs-log interpretation (two combinatorial dimensions of a ring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret the ring structure of a number field as consisting of two underlying 'combinatorial dimensions' corresponding to its additive and multiplicative structures (or unit group vs value group). The Θ-link acts as a 'Θ-dilation' deforming the value-group-like combinatorial dimension while leaving the unit-like combinatorial dimension fixed (up to isomorphism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conceptualizing deformations, view the Θ-link as a Teichmüller-type deformation that dilates one combinatorial dimension (value groups) relative to a Θ-factor while preserving the other (units). This perspective guides how to set up and track deformations in the log-theta-lattice framework (cf. Remark 3.9.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-theta-lattice architecture and noncommutativity of arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-theta-lattice is a two-dimensional diagram of Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters: the 'theta dimension' (Frobenius-picture / Θ-link arrows) and the 'log dimension' (iterated log-link arrows). The Θ-link arrows correspond to mixed-characteristic extension structures of Witt vectors, while log-link arrows correspond to Frobenius morphisms in positive characteristic; these two types of arrows fail to commute (they 'intertwine').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building or analyzing a log-theta-lattice, explicitly mark theta- and log-arrows and account for their failure to commute. Use this interplay to obtain canonical bounds on otherwise 'a priori unbounded deformations' (result claimed in [IUTchIII], Theorem 3.11 and Corollary 3.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical bounds on Θ-deformations from hyperbolicity (target outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Θ-link deformations appear a priori unbounded, in the complete theory (IUTchIII) these deformations admit canonical bounds that reflect the 'hyperbolicity' of the given number field equipped with an elliptic curve; these bounds arise from an explicit description of a varying arithmetic holomorphic structure within a fixed mono-analytic 'container'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to derive canonical bounds for Θ-deformations via the log-theta-lattice formalism and the explicit mono-analytic descriptions (see [IUTchIII], Theorem 3.11 and related remarks). Interpret such bounds as analogues of bounds from differentiating Frobenius liftings in p-adic hyperbolic curve theory.
